comments.body: `containsAny` is evaluated with `.every(...)`, so it means "contains all". The server runs `containsAny` as `&&` (overlap), which means any match (compute-where-condition-parts.ts, `case 'containsAny'`). `isRecordMatchingFilter` calls this for optimistic cache updates (triggerCreateRecordsOptimisticEffect.ts:90, triggerUpdateRecordOptimisticEffect.ts:68). Take a filter "Contains A, B" and a record whose value is [A]. The server returns the record, but the client matcher says it doesn't match. A newly created or updated record is then wrongly left out of the cached list. Use `.some(...)`.

`computeViewRecordGqlOperationFilter` sends `containsIlike` as `%${filter.value}%`, including the SQL wildcards. This matcher lowercases that string and then runs a literal `includes(searchTerm)`, so it looks for the characters `%foo%` inside each item. For a filter value `foo` and a record value `['foo']`, the match is false. The server's ILIKE does match, so optimistic-effect filtering disagrees with the server for ARRAY fields. Strip the `%` characters, or turn the pattern into a regex, before comparing.
